verdicts.flaw_description: The report states throughput at each site 'fell by half against the earlier quarter' and that 'every stack logged here fired in step with site output', so the 8-14 percent lower particulate readings are fully explained by kilns firing half as much, not by the filter upgrade.

The outcome dates precede the intervention: plot One was boxed 3 June but counted 'by 27 March', and plot Three was boxed 2 November but counted 'by 24 September', so those fledgling counts close before the boxes were installed; plot Four (boxed 5 December, counted 21 February) also closes before any fledging season for tawny owls.

The report says 'House air temperature ran a full four degrees above the earlier sowing, and every lot sat on an open bench, taking the house air directly', so a four-degree warmer glasshouse is an alternative cause of the 6-11 point germination gain that applies to all four lots.
The claim is about exam pass rates but every case measures something else: 'coursework submission rates' 7, 5, 8 and 4 points higher. No exam pass rate is reported at all.
